title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-07-10
lineage: AUD > Uher 5 inch open MR > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A rough audience tape that still captures a fiery July 1970 Fillmore East set with incendiary Alligator→The Other One, stellar Not Fade Away and other classic moments.
ai_review.review: Despite the cloudy, hallway‑like audio quality typical of 1970 audience tapes, this recording delivers an energetic performance full of memorable segues – Cold Rain & Snow, the blazing Alligator→The Other One, a gorgeous Attics, and a standout Not Fade Away that showcases Garcia’s melodic blend with Weir. The show is widely praised by reviewers as one of the band’s peak moments in mid‑1970, even if the sound needs listeners’ ears to adjust.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers highlight exceptional musical moments and give high star ratings (4–5) while consistently noting only modest recording flaws; the strong show weighting drives a rating above 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hallway‑like ambience, noticeable crowd clapping near the mic, low‑end emphasis, occasional muddiness (“cloudy, blurry tape”), but overall listenable for a 1970 AUD.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers praise the variety, seamless segues (e.g., Alligator into The Other One) and overall pacing, calling it an exciting snapshot of the band’s 1970 peak.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is highlighted as melodic and ‘mind‑meld’ especially on the Not Fade Away closer.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s snare problems are noted in one review.
